Sub Delete_rows()
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    Application.DisplayAlerts = False
    Dim sh1 As Worksheet
    Dim lastrow As Long
    Set sh1 = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Delete")
    lastrow = sh1.Cells(Rows.Count, "A").End(xlUp).Row
    With sh1
        .AutoFilterMode = False
        .Range("A1:B" & lastrow).AutoFilter Field:=2, Criteria1:=Array("STATIONERY", "VEGETABLES"), Operator:=xlFilterValues
        .Range("A2:C" & lastrow).SpecialCells(xlCellTypeVisible).EntireRow.Delete
        .AutoFilterMode = False
    End With
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    Application.DisplayAlerts = True
End Sub

Circular reference: the formula sits in B323, which is INSIDE the range B$7:B377 that MAX() scans. So B323 depends on MAX(B$7:B377), and that MAX includes B323 itself, so the cell depends on its own value -> circular reference. Excel cannot resolve this, so it returns 0, and with the cell's 000 number format that 0 displays as 000. When you press F9, Excel evaluates just the expression MAX(B$7:B377)+1 against the existing numeric values (the largest is 605), giving 606. Fix: move the formula to a row below the MAX range (e.g. B378) or narrow the range so it does not include the formula cell.
